That evidence supports release robustness in the general case, even though it does not close the named-context coverage gap.
3. On the auditor's concern about whether unresolved named-context gaps permit certification at all: the admissible record does not affirmatively prove a clean certification basis, and I am not claiming it does. My narrower claim is that the same record supports a caveated packet outcome rather than escalation, because the policy concern can be addressed at the packet/disclosure layer by removing the false 'no known limitations' wording and stating the gap as unknown. 4. Model-card wording, certification wording, and monitoring should be kept distinct. ISTRESS-EVAL-COVERAGE-GAP-013-HF-CONTENT supports documenting intended use, limitations, and evaluation results; ISTRESS-EVAL-COVERAGE-GAP-013-NIST-MEASURE supports ongoing measurement and monitoring across deployment. Those authorities support transparent limitation disclosure and post-launch risk handling, but they do not themselves prove the tariff-code context was evaluated.
